newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH CAPITAL MARKETS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH CAPITAL MARKETS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: French bond futures settled slightly lower on Thursday, taking their direction chiefly from Bund futures, and traders said the market was looking somewhat fragile after failing to breach resistance above 129.50 for the second session.

The main focus for the market remained the fluctuations of the dollar/mark parity and continued speculation about if and when the German central bank would either intervene in the currency market or raise short-term rates.
The September contract touched its lows ahead of an auction of long-dated OATs which traders said saw reasonable demand.

The contract survived a test of support around 129.24, climbed with Bunds as the dollar retreated from 1.88 per mark and then got an additional boost from the favourable reaction in the U.S. to minor economic statistics.
Various rumours about the health of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, including talk that he was dead, washed around trading rooms but they were denied by the German government.
Traders said, however, the speculation had weighed on bond prices somewhat in the afternoon session even though the rumours were probably just used to justify a large sell order.
Nevertheless some said they thought there was a risk the contract could return to test 129.02-06 support again on Friday, a level which survived an attack on Wednesday morning.
Traders also said there had been several bearish options strategies on various European bond futures put on, notably by one U.S. house.

The pause in the dollar's appreciation against the mark gave investors some justification for taking some profits on short PIBOR positions, especially the back months which have suffered most during the recent German rate rise speculation.
September 1997 gained one basis point to 96.44 while June 1998 gained five.

Analysts said there had been some shortening of duration ahead of the 30-year bond auction in the United States later on Thursday and the outcome of the sale could have a bearing on European bonds on Friday morning.
The franc was slightly higher against the mark at 3.3728 compared with 3.3745 on Wednesday and up against the dollar at 6.1380 versus 6.3480.
